# Production-Function Estimates for All Industries {#sec-app-pf-all}

The stage-2 estimation in @sec-counterfactual uses the nine industries where overreporting is detected. @tbl-pf-all-industries lists the production-function estimates it uses, with instrument $\tilde{\mathcal W}_{it-2}$. @tbl-overreporting-ratio-all and @fig-overreporting-ratio-all report the distribution of the overreporting ratio for the same nine industries. Beverages (313) appears here but not in @sec-deconvolution or @sec-pf: the variance of its unincorporated firms' residual falls short of the corporations', the condition the deconvolution requires.

## Estimation details {#sec-app-pf-estimation}

The production-function moments in @eq-eta-moments hold for any instrument that is independent of the innovation $\eta_{it}$ and of the measurement errors $\varepsilon_{it}$ and $\varepsilon_{it-1}$. @tbl-orth lists the candidates by the residual they must be orthogonal to. With a single instrument $Z$, the vector $(1,Z,k_{it},l_{it})$ interacted with the residual gives four moments for the four parameters $(\alpha_K,\alpha_L,\gamma_0,\gamma_1)$, and the system is exactly identified. The joint system interacts $(1,m^*_{it-1},\tilde{\mathcal W}_{it-2},k_{it},l_{it})$ with the residual, which gives five moments for the same four parameters. In both systems, $\beta$ stays at its first-stage value, estimated from the corporations' log materials share net of sales taxes, with juridical organization codes 6 to 9 excluded.

Uncertainty comes from test inversion. At each candidate $(\alpha_K,\alpha_L)$ on a 0.005 grid, the parameters $(\gamma_0,\gamma_1)$ are profiled out in closed form, because the problem is linear in $\gamma$ at fixed $\alpha$. With a single instrument, the sharp test compares the statistic with $\chi^2_2$, giving credit for profiling $(\gamma_0,\gamma_1)$, and the conservative test compares it with $\chi^2_4$; with the joint system, the critical values are $\chi^2_3$ and $\chi^2_5$. The grid covers $[0,1]^2$ and extends beyond it in steps of 0.25 wherever a region reaches its edge, down to $-1$ and up to 3. An open bracket marks a region that is not bounded on that side within $[-1,3]^2$, which happens only under $m^*_{it-1}$ and for the conservative region for $\alpha_L$ in Beverages (313). The region for $\beta$ comes from the corporations' share moment alone. With a single instrument, the production-function moments are exactly identified given $\beta$, and profiling them leaves the share moment unchanged.

The point estimate is the minimum of the same statistic whose regions are reported, with the covariance of the moments re-estimated at each candidate. A two-step estimator, which fixes the weighting matrix at a first-step point, understates the statistic when that point fits badly: in Beverages, the joint statistic is 1.62 at the two-step point and 9.96 with the covariance re-estimated there.

The headline instrument is $\tilde{\mathcal W}_{it-2}$ alone. @tbl-pf-instruments compares it with $m^*_{it-1}$ and with the joint system in the five industries of @sec-pf. Across all 28 industries, $\tilde{\mathcal W}_{it-2}$ gives no estimate at a bound of the parameter space and no empty region, and its regions are about as tight as the joint system's: the median width is 0.25 for $\alpha_K$ and 0.35 for $\alpha_L$, against 0.23 and 0.40 for the joint system. On its own, $m^*_{it-1}$ is a weak instrument: its regions for $\alpha_K$ reach 1 in 24 of the 28 industries. The joint sharp region is empty in 311, 312, 313 and 352, where the moments of the two instruments conflict. The untilded $\mathcal W_{it-2}$, which contains $\alpha_Kk_{it-2}+\alpha_Ll_{it-2}$, is not used.

GNR and OLS use the same sample and the same net-of-tax share. The GNR estimates come from an R port of the authors' Stata code, which reproduces it to four decimals.

The distribution of productivity in @sec-pf comes from deconvolving $\tilde{\mathcal W}_{it}=\omega_{it}+(1-\beta)\varepsilon_{it}$ with the corporations' distribution of measurement error, scaled by $1-\beta$, using the estimator of @sec-app-deconvolution. The persistence of productivity is the coefficient $\gamma_1$ from regressing $\tilde{\mathcal W}_{it}$ on $\tilde{\mathcal W}_{it-1}$ with $\tilde{\mathcal W}_{it-2}$ as the instrument, which is independent of the measurement error in the lag, $\varepsilon_{it-1}$. Under GNR, it is the OLS coefficient of $\omega_{it}$ on $\omega_{it-1}$.

Candidate instruments for the production-function moments of @sec-pf, by the residual they must be orthogonal to:

|     |  Orthogonality     |
|:----|:----------------:|
|$\eta_{it}$ | $k_{it},l_{it},\varepsilon_{it}$, $k_{it-1},l_{it-1},\varepsilon_{it-1},\omega_{it-1},\mathcal{W}_{it-1},m_{it-1},m^*_{it-1}$|
| $\varepsilon_{it}$ | $k_{it},l_{it},\omega_{it},m_{it},m^*_{it},\eta_{it}$, $k_{it-1},l_{it-1},\varepsilon_{it-1},\omega_{it-1},\mathcal{W}_{it-1},m_{it-1},m^*_{it-1}$|
| $\varepsilon_{it-1}$ | $k_{it},l_{it},\omega_{it},\varepsilon_{it},m_{it},m^*_{it},\eta_{it}$, $k_{it-1},l_{it-1},\omega_{it-1},\mathcal{W}_{it},m_{it-1},m^*_{it-1}$|
